scenes.title: What is a Chemical Bond?
scenes.explanation: A chemical bond is an attractive and holding force between two atoms, which is the result of the interaction between their electrons.
scenes.narration: A chemical bond is a connection between two atoms that holds them together.
scenes.visual_prompt: An illustration of two atoms with electrons orbiting around them, forming a bond between them.

scenes.title: Types of Chemical Bonds
scenes.explanation: There are several types of chemical bonds, including covalent bonds, ionic bonds, and metallic bonds.
scenes.narration: Chemical bonds come in different types, including covalent bonds, ionic bonds, and metallic bonds.
scenes.visual_prompt: An illustration of a covalent bond, an ionic bond, and a metallic bond, with arrows showing the direction of the bond.

scenes.title: Electronegativity and Polarity
scenes.explanation: Electronegativity is a measure of an atom's ability to attract electrons in a bond. Polarity occurs when the electrons are shared unequally between atoms.
scenes.narration: Electronegativity helps determine how strongly an atom pulls electrons towards itself.
scenes.visual_prompt: An illustration of an atom with a negative charge and another atom with a positive charge, showing the unequal sharing of electrons.

scenes.title: Bonding in Compounds
scenes.explanation: Compounds are formed when atoms share electrons to form bonds. The type of bond and the number of atoms involved determine the properties of the compound.
scenes.narration: Compounds are formed when atoms share electrons to create bonds.
scenes.visual_prompt: An illustration of two atoms sharing electrons to form a covalent bond, with a compound in the background.

scenes.title: Breaking and Forming Bonds
scenes.explanation: Bonds can be broken and formed through chemical reactions. The energy required to break a bond is called the bond dissociation energy.
scenes.narration: Bonds can be broken and formed through chemical reactions, requiring energy.
scenes.visual_prompt: An illustration of a bond being broken and formed, with energy being released or absorbed.
